findings.location: frontierswe::2.description ("each model attempts every task in its own CLI agent harness")
findings.evidence: SOURCE 2 (blog/v2, Methodology/Results) states: "We evaluate each model at its maximum reasoning effort, with Proximus as the default harness and a 20-hour budget per task." SOURCE 1 leaderboard shows a per-row harness label and every listed row carries "proximus" (GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, GLM-5.3, Grok 4.7, Kimi K3, Gemini 3.7 Flash, Qwen3.8-Max, DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision Exp, Muse Spark 1.2, Inkling). SOURCE 6's Harness column is "proximus" for all 13 relay rows. The row's own version_guard likewise asserts "uniform harness proximus". The description's "its own CLI agent harness" therefore reads as per-model native harnesses, which the supplied protocol text does not support and appears to contradict; the only native-harness material in the packet is the separate six-task Proximus-vs-Claude-Code/Codex comparison, not the board. c1 and c2 cannot be satisfied while this identity statement is ambiguous/contradicted.
findings.repair: Reword the description to match the protocol text: each model's runs are executed under the Proximus harness (default harness, 20-hour budget, 5 trials per task), or cite per-model harness coverage only if the packet actually supplies the "Other Harnesses" evidence.

findings.location: frontierswe::2.scoring.notes ("restates 12 overlapping rows byte-exactly"; "proximus is uniform across the main board's 14 rows")
findings.evidence: SOURCE 6 lists 13 relay data rows (claude-fable-5-1, gpt-5.6-sol, glm-5.3, kimi-k3, grok-4.6, gemini-3.7-flash, qwen3.8-max, muse-spark-1.2, Inkling, gpt-6-astra, claude-opus-5, claude-fable-5, gemini-3.8-flash). SOURCE 1's model selector reads "Models: all 16" and enumerates 16 model names, all 13 relay Name values among them (Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-5.6, GLM-5.3, Kimi K3, Grok 4.6, Gemini 3.7 Flash, Qwen3.8-Max, Muse Spark 1.2, Inkling, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5, Claude Fable 5, Gemini 3.8 Flash), while the visible leaderboard table shows 10 rows. Neither the claimed 12-row overlap nor the claimed 14-row main board matches the supplied source counts (13 relay rows; 16 models listed for the board; 10 rows visible). No value in the packet reconciles 12 or 14.
findings.repair: Recount from the sources and correct the figures to the counts actually supported (13 relay rows; board model list of 16 per the site's model selector), or delete the specific counts and state only the harness-uniformity/mapping claim without numbers.

uncertainties: Owner-side hash, transport and qualification checks cannot be executed by this critic; per instructions those are a limitation, not evidence of a defect.

The site excerpt is bounded, so the flight-payload internals asserted in version_guard ("exactly one entries payload", "the abs view carries best/mean/worst with identical row sets") and scoring.notes ("Other Harnesses view") cannot be verified from the packet; the visible leaderboard is truncated at 10 rows so the full board row count is inferred only from the "all 16" model selector.
"restates its mean byte-exactly" cannot be tested: the site shows rounded values (e.g. GLM-5.3 30.2% / Pareto 0.3018 vs relay 0.3018186411764705), so only rounding-level agreement is observable.

The packet does not carry this run's generated added/changed-value summary for this board, so status "active" was judged from protocol text alone (changelog entry dated Sep 22, 2026 adding Claude Opus 5.5; blog states FrontierSWE "will remain an ongoing effort").

The relay's per-model effort is not a dedicated column in the supplied header; it is encoded in Model version suffixes (_max/_xhigh/_high), so "states the per-model effort" is an encoding claim that cannot be fully checked here.
